correctness.rationale: A continuous piecewise-linear median map reduces global induced norms to its strict-order selector matrices. All 120 strict orders yield 60 matrices in eight dihedral orbits, which are checked exactly. Four of six nonwinning classes are strictly Loewner-dominated using 20 exact positive-coefficient leading-principal-minor certificates, another has identical spectrum to a dominated class, and the last is beaten by the positive-root cubic through a strict algebraic substitution. The winners have exact rational and cubic spectral branches. Descartes sign variation certifies a unique positive transversal crossing. Exact executable SymPy reconstruction, not numerical sampling, verifies all nonstandard finite and polynomial identities. Every branch is attained by pairs in a common open chamber.

originality.rationale: The distinctive statement is a full two-input discrete Sobolev operator-norm profile for a periodic 3-point median on five sites with one algebraic switch of attaining rank patterns. The inspected median-filter primary literature covers local rank minimization, statistical risk and output feasibility, rather than this precise two-input norm. Accessible related claims concern sorting, clipping or isotonic projection, whose operator identities do not imply this median-specific spectrum. Search absence is not a novelty proof: equivalent earlier nonlinear-filter or finite matrix results remain possible.

value.rationale: A three-point median on five periodic sites is the first odd local (rather than global-window) case; the complete sharp two-input stability law across all positive gradient penalties is a natural response to sensitivity of robust nonlinear smoothing. It shows an exact, unique change in extremizing order geometry and supplies a nontrivial algebraic benchmark and strong-gradient limit. This is not a textbook application of median contraction or a single arbitrary parameter computation.
